author: The Daily Reflector
title: High school roundup: Jenkins goes deep again to lead Rose softball to win - NewsBreak
text:
By The Daily Reflector ,
14 hours ago
The J.H. Rose softball team broke a 2-2 with a five-run second inning on Wednesday, and those runs stood up for a tight 7-5 win over Ayden-Grifton in non-conference action.
The Chargers scored the games final three runs but could get no closer as Rose improved to 10-1 in its eighth consecutive win.
For the second straight day, Rose's Michelle Jenkins hit a home run and also added a triple and four RBIs. Also for the Rampants, freshman Kayleigh Joyner laced a pair of doubles and drove in two runs.
Rose was set to face Jacksonville on the road on Thursday, while Ayden-Grifton (4-3) travels to Kinston on Friday.
BASEBALL
Greene Central 12, Southside 6
The Rams pounced early and defended their lead in a non-league victory on Wednesday in Chocowinity.
Greene Central (6-3) scored six runs in the first and four more in the second before the Seahawks plated a run. Southside scored four of its six runs in the final two frames but could get no closer.
Sophomore Trey Eatmon was 2-for-2 with four RBIs, fellow sophomore Logan Burress was 3-for-4 with a double and two RBIs, senior Riley Radford drove in two and sophomore Sutton Harris doubled and scored two runs for the Rams.
GC will look for a third straight win on Friday at Tarboro.
John Paul II 4, Rocky Mount Academy 2
The Saints made it three wins in the last four on Wednesday when they made an early lead stand and got a strong combined pitching performance.
Senior JT Williams homered, doubled, drove in two and finished 3-for-4. Junior Kaden Knight added an RBI double.
On the mound, junior Adam Donofrio went 4.1 innings, struck out seven, walked two and allowed two runs on two hits before Williams took the ball the rest of the way, yielding no runs while also fanning seven and walking two.
JPII traveled to Richlands on Thursday to take on Liberty Christian before hosting Wilson Christian on April 2.
SouthWest Edgecombe 6, Farmville Central 3
The Jaguars rallied to tie the Cougars early on but could not withstand a second late surge on Wednesday.
SWE scored the runs in the top of the first inning, but Farmville counteredwith one in the bottom of the first and two more in the third to knot the score. But the hosts had no answer when the Cougars broke the impasse in a three-run sixth.
The Jags managed just two hits but allowed only four, though FC committed three errors.Connor Kessler's solo home run was one of those hits and the other was Chase Felton's two-run double.
Farmville hosts Beddingfield on Friday in Eastern Plains Conference action.
C.B. Aycock 6, Ayden-Grifton 0
The Chargers were pinned with their initial loss of the season on Wednesday night against a Golden Falcons club that won just its third game in 10 tries.
No stats were reported.
Ayden-Grifton (9-1) plays at Kinston on Friday.
Ayden-Grifton 15-18, Kinston 0-1
On Tuesday night, Ayden-Grifton completed a dominant doubleheader sweep at home against the Vikings, marking their eighth and ninth wins in as many tries.
In the 15-0 opener, the Chargers scored eight runs in the first inning to set the tone and seven combined over the next two to put the game on the path to a five-inning shutout.
A-G belted out nine hits to Kinston's one. Junior Brysen Williams tripled and drove in two runs, junior Zach Jones was 3-for-3 with two RBIs and seniors John Fields and Daniel Colby also drove in a pair each for the Chargers.
On the mound, Jones and senior Joshua Steelman combined for a solid shutout outing that included 11 strikeouts and one walk between them.
In the 18-1 romp, A-G opened the game with three straight six-run innings before Kinston countered with a lone run in the fourth inning of another five-inning game.
Steelman laced a pair of doubles and drove in three runs to pace the Chargers and junior James Allen added a double and four RBIs. Junior Tucker Vaughn added two hits and two RBIs, and Colby drove in three to cap a five-RBI day.
Junior Adam Smith struck out five and walked none in two shutout innings before sophomore Anderson Watkins struck out the side in his one frame and junior Hunter Hollingsworth threw the final two, also striking out five and walking none.
